answer: I'd like to talk about a meal that, for me, sums up what Eid is really about. A special meal that stands out in my memory was a large family feast during Eid last year, prepared mostly by my mother and grandmother. We celebrated at my grandparents' home in our ancestral village, and the whole extended family gathered there, which is increasingly rare these days. My elder sister came from Dhaka with her husband and children, and my uncles and cousins came too. My job was to help my grandfather greet the guests and make sure everyone had a seat. The table was [[laden with]] traditional dishes, like beef curry, chicken roast, polao and several kinds of sweets, and the aromas alone were [[mouthwatering]]. What made the meal so special was not just the food, though it was absolutely delicious, but the sense of togetherness. We spent hours eating, talking and laughing, with several generations gathered around one table, from my grandfather in his eighties to my four-year-old nephew. There is something deeply [[comforting]] about a home-cooked meal shared with people you love. In our busy lives, such [[unhurried]] gatherings feel genuinely precious. I remember feeling completely content, surrounded by family and good food. After lunch, the older men sat in the courtyard drinking tea while the children played. Honestly, meals like that are about far more than eating; they are about connection and belonging. It is a [[treasured]] memory, and it reminds me that the best meals are the ones shared with the people who matter most. I am already looking forward to the next Eid.

followUps.q: Can you cook any of those dishes yourself?
followUps.answer: Only a simple chicken curry, I am afraid. The Eid dishes take real skill and a lot of time, so I leave them to my mother and grandmother and happily do the washing up instead.

followUps.q: Do you prefer eating at home or in restaurants?
followUps.answer: At home, definitely. Restaurants are nice for a change, but nothing compares to my mother's cooking, and eating together at home feels far more relaxed and personal.
